items.title: Identifying True Statements About Limits

sections.normalized_html:
Which of the following statements are true concerning the function [MATH: y=f(x)] whose graph is shown below?

  1. [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,0}f(x)=0]

  2. [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,3}f(x)=0]

  3. [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-1}f(x)=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,1}f(x)]
sections.readable_text:
Which of the following statements are true concerning the function [MATH: y=f(x)] whose graph is shown below?

1. [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,0}f(x)=0]
2. [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,3}f(x)=0]
3. [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-1}f(x)=\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,1}f(x)]

[IMG: /graphics/42148299c32a941ad027d9e49c2933f7]

sections.normalized_html:
Let's analyze each statement in turn.

  • Statement I is false. As [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 0,] the function [MATH: f(x)] approaches the value [MATH: y=-1.] Consequently, [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,0}f(x)=-1.]

  • Statement II is true. As [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 3,] the function [MATH: f(x)] approaches the value [MATH: y=0.] Consequently, [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,3}f(x)=0.]

  • Statement III is false. As [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: -1] the function [MATH: f(x)] approaches the value [MATH: y=2,] and consequently [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-1}f(x)=2.] Similiarly, as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 1,] the function [MATH: f(x)] approaches the value [MATH: y=-2,] and consequently [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,1}f(x)=-2.] As a result, [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,-1}f(x)\ne\lim_\limits{x\rightarrow \,1}f(x).]

In conclusion, only statement II is true.

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
The limit of a function is the value that the function approaches. For example, the function [MATH: y=f(x)] shown below is not defined at [MATH: x=2,] as represented by the open circle there [MATH: -] but when we approach [MATH: x=2], we see that [MATH: f(x)] approaches the value [MATH: y=1.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/771b75fb2f377e3f83070583105136a1]

Content:
As [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 2], the value of [MATH: f(x)] approaches [MATH: 1.] In other words, the limit of [MATH: f(x),] as [MATH: x] approaches [MATH: 2,] is [MATH: 1]. We can express this mathematically as [MATH: \lim_\limits{x\rightarrow 2}f(x)=1 \, .]
